title: Pleasing God · Chapter 6: The Blessings of a God Pleaser
speaker: Joshua Heward-Mills
text:
Chapter 6

# The Blessings of a God Pleaser

Why please God? What’s the point? How does it help you? How does it change your life? One of the reasons why you should make it your aim to please God is that He received from the Father honour and glory.

# a. Honour and glory.

For he received from God the Father honour and glory, when there came such a voice to him from the excellent glory, This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased.

2 Peter 1:17 (KJV)

Jesus received honour and glory from the Father when the voice declared pleasure in Him. God's approval carries something greater than human applause. He can place honour on a life that once looked disordered and unattractive.

I remember being called forward at school for punishment. Later I heard my name announced before congregations welcoming me to minister. God had done something in a life that had once been very different. His honour is not the same as simply making yourself impressive.

# b. You discover the purpose for which you were made.

Thou art worthy, O Lord, to receive glory and honour and power: for thou hast created all things, and for thy pleasure they are and were created.

Revelation 4:11 (KJV)

We were created for His pleasure. A life used for something other than its purpose becomes strained and disordered.

A vehicle used continually on terrain it was not designed for will suffer. A fish put on a road cannot compete with a person running there. Put both in water, and the fish moves freely in the place for which it was made. Purpose makes a difference.

For me to have remained in a career God was calling me out of would have been to use my life against its purpose. The issue was not that every person must leave that profession. The issue was what He had created and called me to do.

# c. There is provision and satisfaction in submission.

The haters of the LORD should have submitted themselves unto him: but their time should have endured for ever. He should have fed them also with the finest of the wheat: and with honey out of the rock should I have satisfied thee.

Psalm 81:15-16 (KJV)

God speaks of the submission that should have been given to Him and the satisfaction He would have supplied. Honey out of the rock is a striking picture. What looks hard and unpromising can become a place of provision when we are before Him.

Do not build your life around every impulse: shouting because you are angry, pursuing a desire because it is strong, or choosing whatever seems best to you without Him. Submit the life to its Maker.

# d. Pleasing Him belongs to true service.

For do I now persuade men, or God? or do I seek to please men? for if I yet pleased men, I should not be the servant of Christ.

Galatians 1:10 (KJV)

Serving God is not simply doing a little preaching or church work while reserving the rest of life for self-will.

Neither yield ye your members as instruments of unrighteousness unto sin: but yield yourselves unto God, as those that are alive from the dead, and your members as instruments of righteousness unto God.

Romans 6:13 (KJV)

An instrument is a utensil, a tool. It's used by God. To serve God is to please Him. It's not just to preach. It's to say, “What do You need? Tell me where You want me to go. I will obey You, Lord.” That's what it means to be a servant of God.

# e. Answered prayer.

And whatsoever we ask, we receive of him, because we keep his commandments, and do those things that are pleasing in his sight.

1 John 3:22 (KJV)

The verse connects receiving what we ask with keeping His commandments and doing what is pleasing in His sight. We should not ignore that connection while asking why our prayers seem unanswered.

In a family, children sometimes know which sibling is best placed to make a request because that child has been doing the things that please the parents. Consider your own conduct before God as well as the request you are bringing.

# f. Peace with enemies.

When a man’s ways please the LORD, he maketh even his enemies to be at peace with him.

Proverbs 16:7 (KJV)

Instead of making the destruction of your enemies your chief concern, attend to pleasing God. He is able to make even opposition come to peace with you. Their hostility is not beyond His reach.

# g. A name that is not forgotten.

The Lord says, “Suppose some eunuchs keep my Sabbath days. They choose to do what pleases me. And they are faithful in keeping my covenant. Then I will set up a monument in the area of my temple. Their names will be written on it. That will be better for them than having sons and daughters. The names of the eunuchs will be remembered forever. They will never be forgotten.

Isaiah 56:4-5 (NIrV)

God's promise here reaches beyond the ordinary ways people try to secure remembrance. Choosing what pleases Him and keeping His covenant matters more than the human arrangements on which we depend for a lasting name.

Famous people can be forgotten remarkably quickly. A generation may barely recognise names that once filled the news. Yet I have seen a chapel on the West African coast bearing the name of Wesley, a man from another country and another century. God's service can have a reach beyond what a person arranged for himself.

# h. Needs supplied.

But I have all, and abound: I am full, having received of Epaphroditus the things which were sent from you, an odour of a sweet smell, a sacrifice acceptable, wellpleasing to God. But my God shall supply all your need according to his riches in glory by Christ Jesus.

Philippians 4:18-19 (KJV)

Paul described the Philippians' gift as well pleasing to God and then spoke of God's supply. The giver's relation to God was larger than the immediate transaction with Paul.

Giving also reaches towards the brother or sister in need.

But whoever has the world’s goods, and sees his brother in need and closes his heart against him, how does the love of God abide in him?

1 John 3:17 (NASB 1995)

The liberal soul shall be made fat: and he that watereth shall be watered also himself.

Proverbs 11:25 (KJV)

The liberal soul reflects a way of thinking: I should help; I should share; I should join in meeting this need. That disposition matters.

The thought that I should give, that I should join, that I should help—it’s a way of thinking. A giving mind, an idea that we should give to other people, will always be blessed.

The thoughts of the righteous are right: but the counsels of the wicked are deceit.

Proverbs 12:5 (KJV)

But to do good and to communicate forget not: for with such sacrifices God is well pleased.

Hebrews 13:16 (KJV)

Doing good and sharing are sacrifices with which God is pleased.
